title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: how an invoice dispute is lodged and decided
content:
## Scope

This policy of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category governs disputes against a single invoice line of a per-container record: who may dispute, the dispute window, how many disputes a line may carry, the grounds the desk decides from its records, and the status needed for a credit.

## Policy clauses

1. The billed party may dispute one invoice line, and only the billed party can do so. The dispute is lodged by the customer and decided by the desk within the product's decision period.
2. The dispute must be lodged no later than the product's dispute window in calendar days after the disputed invoice was issued. The window ends on the invoice date plus the product's window days, counted on calendar dates, and a dispute lodged on the last day is in time.
3. An invoice line carries at most one dispute. An earlier dispute on the line counts when it is submitted, upheld, partially upheld or denied.
4. A credit may be booked only on a record whose status is invoiced.
5. A disputed invoice is not due while its dispute is submitted.

The window runs from the invoice line's own date and is compared with the time the dispute was registered; both are taken from the line's records.

## Grounds and how the desk decides them

| Ground | Decided from the desk's records? | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| invoice issued late | yes | The invoice is upheld as not collectible when its date is later than the record's clock-stop date plus the product's invoice issue deadline in days. No dispute credit is written for this ground. |
| rate misapplied, free time misapplied | yes | The desk recomputes the invoice line under the invoicing rules with the product and recorded dates of the record. When the invoiced amount exceeds the recomputed amount, the dispute is upheld or partially upheld and credited by a dispute credit of the difference, but never more than the disputed amount; when it does not, the dispute is denied and nothing is booked. |
| incorrect event dates, carrier-caused delay, terminal closure | no | These turn on operational facts the desk's records do not hold; the desk registers them and cannot decide them. |

## Late invoice clearance

- "On the invoice-issued-late ground, the whole amount still open on the invoice is cleared by a waiver recorded as a late invoice." This clause is **no longer in force** as the basis for clearing a late demurrage invoice line; the current late-demurrage clearance basis replaces it there.
- The same late-invoice waiver clears a late invoice raised by the customer without a formal dispute.
- The amount still open on an invoice line is its amount less the waivers and dispute credits already booked against that line before the entry being handled.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical; an illustrative window of 20 days is used only to show the counting)

| Invoice date | Last day of the illustrative window | Dispute lodged | In time? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 May | 21 May | 21 May | yes |
| 1 May | 21 May | 22 May | no, the window condition is not met |

## Points of judgement

**Q: A consignee disputes a line on the ground of a terminal closure. Can the desk decide it?**
A: No. The desk registers such a dispute and cannot decide it.

**Q: The line's only earlier dispute was denied. May a second dispute be lodged?**
A: No. A denied dispute counts toward the one dispute a line may carry.
